newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia debt data happy, fret over Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia debt data happy, fret over Greenspan.

text.p: *Australian bonds failed to sustain the relief rally that followed today's wage agreements data as the market braced itself for the Humphrey-Hawkins testimony later today.
*Final average weekly earnings, capex due Thursday.

Australian bonds failed to sustain the relief rally that followed today's wage agreements data as the market braced itself for U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony.
"I think the market got carried away with the figure and are obviously concerned about Greenspan. It has been a long time since he's said anything bullish," said one local bond trader.
However, the data was one obstacle the market was happy to get over and helped to soothe recent concerns over potential wage pressures harming the current benign inflation outlook.

"There are uncertainties on the wages front and upside risks to wages growth in the longer term. Add to this fact that all signs point to a strengthening economy on the horizon, today's data are unlikely to sway the RBA's 'rates on hold' strategy," said Su-Lin Ong, fixed income economist at Hambros Bank.

The market faces more news on wages with final average weekly ordinary time earnings due on Thursday, along with another instalment in the fourth quarter GDP saga with the release of capital expenditure for the quarter.
The overall GDP report is due on March 5.

The market's afternoon set back saw long-dated spreads reverse the tightening to the dollar bloc that was seen just after the data. However, the short-end showed a net outperformance on the day, and the yield curve steepened with the three/10-year spread at its highest level for three weeks.
